metadata.description: Pass the baton from Claude Code or Codex to a local DeepSeek Harness. An MCP server that hands off tasks and brings the result back.
metadata.name: dsh-baton

paragraphs.text: Pass the baton from Claude Code or Codex to a local DeepSeek Harness. An MCP server that hands off t
asks and brings the result back.
Quick start  ·  See it run  ·  How it compares  ·  Token usage  ·  How it works  ·  Tools  ·  Securi
ick start  ·  See it run  ·  How it compares  ·  Token usage  ·  How it works  ·  Tools  ·  Security
Hand coding tasks from Claude Code or Codex to DeepSeek Harness on your machine: the task runs live
in the Harness window, the main agent hears back once when it ends, and it gets back the files that
changed, the project's own test results and a requirement-by-requirement checklist.
- **Watch it and step in:** the task runs live in the Harness window and you can type into it at any
time. Every message is labelled "Sent by ChatGPT / Claude from another chat". When Harness stops to
ask a question, the main agent answers it if you told it to decide, or brings it to you with its ow

n recommendation.
- **Less of the 5-hour window:** a long Codex job takes 16% of a ChatGPT Plus 5-ho
ur window instead of 86% (GPT-6 Astra, the kanban task). The rest of the numbers are under Token usa

ge.
- **Nothing to watch or poll:** the main agent waits without polling and gets the result when th
e run ends. With several runs going at once, each one comes back within a second of finishing.
Needs DeepSeek Harness ≥ 0.2.1-rc.2 (signed in) and Claude Code or Codex. Quick start →
## What it is
dsh-baton is an MCP server plus a small Harness plugin. The main agent hands the task to an ordinary
Harness session with one tool call: you watch it run in the Harness window and can step in at any t
ime, and the main agent hears back once, without polling. Unlike a plain MCP bridge to another model
, the work stays visible and the proof comes back with the result.
## How it compares
|  | **dsh-baton** | Model-swap gateway | Background sub-agent |
| The main agent keeps its own model | **Yes** | No, the whole chat runs on the other model | Yes |
| You can watch the work | **Yes, live in the Harness window** | Yes, in the same chat | The main ch

at gets a summary |
| You can step in mid-run | **Yes, in Harness, or the main agent steers it in**

| Yes | Usually not |
| Each message says who sent it | **Yes, sent by ChatGPT / Claude** | One side

only | Not needed |
| Changed files and test results come back | **dsh-baton lists the files and ru

ns your tests itself** | No hand-over step | The sub-agent's own summary |
| Questions reach you | *
*Yes, with the main agent's recommendation** | It asks you directly | Usually not |
## Why split the work
Beyond the savings, the split itself helps:
- **A spec before the code.** The main agent turns your loose request into clear requirements before

handing it over, so Harness gets a clear spec rather than a relayed "build me an X".
- **Checked on
evidence.** The result carries the changed files, your project's own test output and a point-by-poi
nt check against the request; anything missing goes back for another round, instead of taking "done"

on trust.
- **The main conversation keeps the decisions.** Hundreds of steps of reading files, edit
ing and running tests stay in the Harness session; the main conversation holds your request and the
ing tests stay in the Harness session; the main conversation holds your request and the conclusions.
## Quick start
**Install in one step, check in two.**
Nothing else to install: no Node.js, no terminal. It is the same on macOS and Windows.
**Install:** in Harness, **Plugins** (插件) → **Add plugin** (添加插件) → type `dsh-baton-host` → **Instal
l** (安装) → **Enable now** (立即启用). Switched on, the plugin registers dsh-baton for Claude Code and Co
dex, for every folder, and Harness says so.
**Check that it works:**
① **Open a new chat:** in Claude Code or Codex, start a **new** conversation; one that was already o
pen does not see dsh-baton yet. It is the same in both. Codex asks you to approve MCP tool calls: ap
prove the `dsh-baton` tools (for unattended `codex exec` runs, add `--approve-for-me`).
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
**Pick a model:** just say which one, for example "hand it to DeepSeek, V4 Pro". `dsh_send` passes i
t as `model` (and `reasoning_effort`), matched against the models Harness lists, so a model Harness
adds later works as soon as it shows up. It applies to that session only; Harness's default model st
ays as it was. `dsh_list_models` shows what is available.
**Answering Harness's questions:** the main agent answers the way the task needs, rather than pickin
g the least bad option. See `dsh_answer` under Tools.
**Several runs at once.** When a task is split across sessions, the main agent sends them all and wa
its for them together; whichever ends first comes back first, so it can review it and send a fix whi
le the rest still run.
**Sessions with a Harness goal.** A session with a goal (set by a message starting with `/goal`) sta
rts its next round by itself; dsh-baton waits until the goal stops before handing back, and can repo
rt progress at an interval you ask for.
Waiting in detail: each client, several runs, goals, changing the request
- **Claude Code** waits for a run in the background (the `wait_command` that `dsh_send` returns) and

is woken once, when the run ends.
- **Codex** waits inside `dsh_wait`. The plugin sets Codex's tool
timeout for dsh-baton to an hour (`tool_timeout_sec = 3600`), so one call waits up to 59 minutes: a
run that ends within the hour costs one model request to wait for, however long it takes, and the r
esult comes back as an ordinary tool result in the chat. A longer run returns `timed_out` with just
the state after 59 minutes, and Codex calls again without summarising. Pressing Stop ends the wait a
t once. Codex gets no `wait_command`: its terminal cannot wake it, so it would poll. A conversation
without that setting waits 270 s per call. Measured in the Codex desktop app: a 28-minute run took o
ne `dsh_wait` call; a 62-minute run took two, the first returning `timed_out` after 59 minutes and t

he second getting the result 3 minutes later, with no `dsh_status` calls in between.
[该节后续省略]
## Security and limits
Any process running as your OS user can drive Harness through the socket, the same as running `dsh`
directly. dsh-baton relies on Harness's internal service APIs (0.2.1 and 0.2.2 today), so a major Ha
rness update may need a follow-up release.
